title: The Second Temple
lead: The Second Temple is the house rebuilt in Jerusalem after the exile, finished in March 515 BC under the governor Zerubbabel and the high priest Joshua (Ezra 6:15), and later expanded by Herod. It is the setting of Haggai and Zechariah 1-8.

sections.b: Cyrus allowed the rebuilding in 538 BC (Ezra 1:1-4), the altar and a foundation were set under Zerubbabel and Jeshua (Ezra 3), the work stopped (Ezra 4:24) and began again in 520 on the preaching of Haggai and Zechariah (Ezra 5:1-2; Haggai 1:12-15). It was finished in the sixth year of Darius (Ezra 6:15) and dedicated with joy (Ezra 6:16-18). The old people wept at the foundation, comparing it with Solomon's (Ezra 3:12-13; Haggai 2:3).
sections.refs: Ezra 1:1-4; Ezra 3:8-13; Ezra 4:24; Ezra 5:1-2; Ezra 6:14-18; Haggai 1:12-15; Haggai 2:3

sections.b: Haggai promises that the last glory will be greater than the first (Haggai 2:9). Jewish tradition says five things the first Temple had were missing from the second: the ark, the fire, the Shekhinah, the Holy Spirit, and the Urim and Thummim (Bavli Yoma 21b). Herod rebuilt and enlarged the Temple from about 20 BC, and Josephus describes it (Antiquities 15.380-425). It was destroyed in AD 70.
